newsitem.title: FINLAND: Topics cover broad spectrum at Finnish Latin-fest.
newsitem.headline: Topics cover broad spectrum at Finnish Latin-fest.

text.p: The guttural chants of Siberian tribes, funeral rites for bears and the views of writers throughout history on flying lurk among the diverse topics that Latin-language devotees will discuss at a conference in Finland this week.
About 230 delegates from 22 countries will attend the "conventus internationalis" in the language that runs in the central Finnish town of Jyvaskyla until next Tuesday.
They include students as young as 16 as well as academics and writers, conference chairman Tuomo Pekkanen said on Thursday.
"For us, Latin is a living language and very good fun," he said in a telephone interview. "I've been speaking it for 42 years and I like to speak it every day."

A concert of ancient Finnish songs performed to mark the funeral rites of bears provides one subject. "I translated the original verses from Finnish into Latin to make them accessible to an international audience," Pekkanen said.
The event also features a jazz arrangement of the poems of Catullus. But a Finnish professor who records Latin versions of Elvis Presley hits failed to make the programme.
Held in Finland, the only country where state radio broadcasts regular news bulletins in Latin, the congress is sponsored by the Rome-based Latin Academy.
All the speeches are being given in Latin but delegates are not forbidden from also using "modern languages from greater Europe", Pekkanen said.

"De insania volandi quid Latini scriptores senserint", a talk to be given by celebrated German Latinist Walahfridus Stroh, is not about insane desires but discusses what Latin writers thought about flying, he explained.
